text: Everyyyyyone told me to come to Ruby Slipper Cafe when I came back to visit NOLA once more. Why? Is a question that lingers. My friend Kirby, a NOLA Native, also suggested Ruby Slipper Cafe and then I knew that perhaps, this was a place to put on my list. With numerous locations, I feared the wait would match that of the Canal St. location where I observed crowds of guests waiting outdoors for seating. Luckily at the Broad St. location, we seemingly walked right in. Busy and filled with guests on a Sunday morning, I figured I was in for a real treat after all of the recommendations passed onto me. We were seated at a small booth in the back and awaited our waitress. After waiting about 15 minutes, we were finally greeted and placed our drink orders. 10 minutes later, we got drinks. This seemed to be the routine of the morning, as the service received was spaced out and nothign to write home about. Because Kirby and I are both former servers, we understand the pros and cons of serving and try not to be critical but were quite dissapointed that we struggled to get our servers attention despite the lack of fuss happening in her section. Despite that, we continued to focus on our meal. Kirby opted for French Toast with an extra side of Bacon, "not fried crispy, but soft" and as a pregnant woman, I know she meant this. I ordered a Croque Madame with a side of bacon as well and we waited with baited breath, hoping our meals would come fast enough to keep Kirby, the baby and myself in good spirits -- and from eating someone elses food on a neighboring table. When our food finally arrived to our table about 15-20 min. later, we were both starving and planned to dive right in. Upon review of our food as I was snapping some shots, we realized that the bacon Kirby previously requested be "not fried crispy, but soft" as her cravings desired, was almost as black as the boots I was wearing. It's almost like the server didn't pass the memo on at all. When we finally got ahold of her, we promptly sent the bacon back and continued our meals. Kirby was a big fan of her French Toast and the bacon they finally did bring out. My Croque Madame, not so much but this was my first experience trying one. I think that I expected something sweet and savory, but the bread was dryer than expected vs. being soft to the bite, although I appreciate the huge slices. Overall, my experience simply fell short of what I expected. I don't find myself loving chain food too much and believed Ruby Slipper to be different... but maybe another try will prove me wrong?

text: On Bluff Road (just south of I-465 on the southwest side) one of the remaining retail greenhouses is still doing quite well. A driveway on the north of the building is the one to pull into and allows you to head along the rest of the buildings where you can park by pulling into the angle parking or using the larger lot near the rear. There are flatbed wagons that you can use to load your plant selections on while you browse through the sheds. If you are getting more than one of an item, you can make use of the plastic shipping trays to load your choices so that they are less likely to fall off your cart. Generally speaking, you will find veggies to the north of the first shed, perennials in the next few, and annuals towards the rear. The plants we have purchased over the years have looked very healthy and well cared for. The staff is generally helpful in finding a specific type of plant, but even they can be stumped sometimes and may need to ask one of their coworkers. Still, they have good teamwork and are willing to help you find what you want. All in all, a nice selection of plants. text: MEXICAN FOOD EMERGENCY Working on the road is not always glamorous for example my day started at 5am with breakfast at a Starbucks in Hammond, Indiana. Fast forward to midnight and I've worked all day without a proper meal. Typically I'm going to go to bed hungry because there aren't many food options on the road past 10pm, unless you want crappy fast food. I truly love my Yelp app because it's there for me during food emergencies. I'm always using my filters based on my needs. Tonight I used "Open Now" which helps me filter through my available food options. I don't need to start reading 5 star reviews about a place that is closed at midnight. That never helps and I just get HANGRY!This place immediately showed up and was only 0.9 miles from my hotel. The best part is they were even open 24/7 which also gets a lifetime bookmark from me in case of another midnight Mexican Food Emergency. When I drove up I noticed four guys eating inside which is always a good sign. Empty restaurants feel scary. I also noticed the restaurant had a drive thru too which I may use on my next visit. When I went inside my eyes got huge. Everything on the menu looked fantastic. Remember I had Starbucks for breakfast about 19 hours ago. There's a good chance I'm ordering the whole menu board. I decided to get the Steak Burrito which comes the way I totally love it with just pico de gallo and guacamole. Score! I also added on an order of the chicken enchiladas. While I was waiting for my order to be made the guy at the counter pointed me to the self serve salsa bar! I was so happy to see this. I was carrying out and I packed three salsa verde, two mild red and two hot red salsas. They even provided little lunch baggies just in case you didn't put the lid on right and it opened up on your way home. I call that Salsa Safety! On a side note another Yelper blasted this place for not having any salsa. I feel bad for them because the free self serve salsa was right in the dining room. I'm not sure how you could miss this Mecca of Salsa. I loved both the medium spicy verde and the mild red salsa. I carried out my food because it's sad to eat alone at midnight plus no one can see you pigging out in your hotel room. The steak burrito was wonderful. This is how I like it. It was so simple. Grilled steak along with fresh guac and pico wrapped in a grilled burrito is the bomb. This is the only way to have it. The chicken in the enchiladas was nice too. The white meat was shredded and moist. The red enchilada sauce was also tasty and rich. I enjoyed the salad on top too. This makes the dish healthy. Right? I would definitely come back especially for late night food. Was the food here life changing? Nope but it's good Mexican. I throughly enjoyed every bite and it saved me from going to bed or eating at a gas station. Ironically before stopping here I almost bought a ramen bowl at the gas station up the road. I'm honestly glad I didn't because this meal was much better. Desperation truly sets in when your tired and hungry. I'm glad I found this 24/7 restaurant. I will always visit you at midnight when I'm working in the area. I might even use that drive thru now that I know what to order.

text: 2 months ago we paid $4000 for peace of mind to have a snake fence installed by Arizona Snake Fence Company on our backyard preserve fence. We did not want to worry about rattlesnakes in our yard. The company advertises that they provide "post-install snake removals", "post-install inspection to meet all tolerance requirements necessary to meet a safe area", and a "free warranty"; all of which also made us feel that this was a very good investment. Initially, we felt secure in our backyard after the fence installation. Earlier this week I was frightened when I came within 1 foot of a coiled rattlesnake in our backyard! Thankfully, I was not bitten. It was on our side of the fence (see photo with snake fence behind the snake)! It should be noted that we never leave our side gate propped open, and there have been no tradesmen working in our back yard since the snake fence was installed who could have possibly "tampered" with our fence in anyway (this was the suggestion of the snake fence company's owner). Home alone, I panicked, and tried to call and email the snake fence company a few times that day to remove the rattlesnake from our yard. Unfortunately I only reached their answering machine, and had to then obtain another service to remove the snake from my backyard. The owner of the company did eventually call me back later that day, and stated that he would come out to check the fence the next day. But, at that time (even before visualizing the fence in person) he suggested possible causes other than fault with their fence installation. When he did come to my home to check the fence the next day, he pushed down some fencing wire with pliers, that I had pointed out to him of openings that looked large enough for a snake to slide through. He did this along 3 - 4 grout line areas under the fence, where the fence bottom meets the block wall. He at first said that the snake could have possibly entered in those small opening areas. Later in the conversation, he stated that he thought that the snake could have been actually hiding in our yard for the last 2 months (prior to them doing the fence), and they "may have missed it during the fence installation", or that our side gate had been left open too long by someone to allow the snake to enter from the front yard and the road, because he didn't actually think it came in through from the backyard preserve through the small identified openings below the fence that I had pointed out to him. He also stated that he didn't see any "tampering" by others of my fence. My husband and I were then floored when he charged us a service call for the visit! The company touts a "free 1 year warranty" on their website. But I was told that even after spending $4000 just two months ago for his services, that our request for him to come out post-install after a live rattlesnake showed up in our yard to assess our safety, the security of the fence, and to restore our peace of mind was not covered under the free "warranty". We are very disappointed in the customer service (or lack of) that was provided by the owner of Arizona Snake Fence.

text: I first came to Cafe Roze when it was fairly new. I went during the day and just for a tea. It was a nice experience overall and I have wanted to return for awhile. My mother and friend were in town visiting and were staying in East Nashville. We wanted a cocktail and dinner so I suggested Cafe Roze. It was such a different vibe at night and provided the most lovely evening for our group. We arrived around 7:30 and were able to get a table right away. At night, the lights are dim with a glow coming from the Cafe Roze pink neon sign. The cafe itself is pretty small with bar seating and a long wood bench along the wall. The decor is simple yet elegant. Think gold light fixtures, marble tables, and pastel colors. We each ordered a cocktail and then decided to share appetizers so we could try a few different things. I got the melon cocktail and it was delicious. The size was larger than other places. We then ordered the apps one at a time. The first one to come out was the beet toast. I'm not a beet person but this was so good. The dill flavor really made it amazing. Next, we ordered the avocado hummus and parmesan corn fritters. Wow. That hummus is insanely good. It has a mousse texture so it's really light. It is served with toasted bread. I think we licked the bowl clean. Get this. The fritters were also really good. A nice cheesy parmesan flavor. The last thing we tried was the miso cauliflower. I only had a few bites of this because I was already so full, but the flavor was great. I'm always amazed how good cauliflower can be. The texture was nice and the miso flavoring was the perfect amount. My mom and her friend could not stop talking about how much they loved Cafe Roze. It's a very relaxed and chic atmosphere. The perfect night with amazing food and drinks!

They told me it would cost $25 per person for a meal that, on any other Sunday, would have been much less - although they did throw in a beverage and a muffin or fruit cup... So, when we got there, they had packed the small place with too many tables, most of which had families seated at them. Our waiter even commented on the "close quarters." We got our beverages and "complimentary" muffins, danishes and fruit cups. Our breakfast order was taken about twenty minutes after arrival. And we didn't receive our food until an hour and fifteen minutes after arrival. (Let that sink in for a moment...) Tables whose orders were taken after ours got their food before us, too. When it did arrive, the food was mediocre and lacking in flavor. Our waiter came out towards the end to commiserate about how busy they were and apologize for the slow service. He then made a comment that the next seating would not be allowed any modifications to menu items. (Our table had asked for a couple of minor modifications to the meals - i.e. "no tomatoes" - so this was obviously aimed at us.) We heard other tables complaining about the food and service. It's really a shame that a restaurant that people seem to like (based on the positive reviews) would try to capitalize on Mother's Day by over-charging and over-stuffing the restaurant with too many customers at once, putting a strain on the kitchen and servers and causing sub-par food to be served unacceptably slowly. I will not be returning.

text: STRONG CAUTION AGAINST USING THIS FACILITY! Although there may have been a few positive highlights, the majority of the experience that my family had with Casas Adobes Post Acute Rehabilitation (Skilled Nursing Facility) was absolutely AWFUL! To be clear, my mother was discharged from the hospital to this facility during COVID, therefore I understand the need for no visitors. However, with that being the case, one would think that the communication between the staff and the patient's families would be of the utmost priority, which it most certainly was NOT. Especially considering the fact that the patient has communication issues due to previous strokes and has a diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment - that makes it even more important to COMMUNICATE WITH THE FAMILY! In addition to the communication being a major issue, my 90 lb. mother fell THREE TIMES while in the care of this facility...even though she was marked as a fall risk in the hospital. I still do not understand how that can happen! Furthermore, she lost her partial one-tooth denture during the first week of her stay. After trying to figure out what happened or how they could replace it, I was basically told that there was nothing they could do. Coupled with the utter lack of communication, the processes of rehabilitation, therapy, discharge, and transfer to an assisted living facility were not broken down or explained to our family at all. We were consistently given the runaround, calls and emails were not returned, and the process was made a lot more stressful than I believe it needed to be. In addition, one family member needed to provide documentation to his employer in order for his leave time to be approved for helping to handle my mother's affairs. The staff at Casas Adobes led us to believe that it would be no problem to have that filled out; yet after having the paperwork for TWO WEEKS, it was returned to us incomplete, causing our family member to be penalized. If I have learned anything while advocating for my mother, it is that I wish there had been more reviews like this when I was researching facilities for her. My family and I chose Casas Adobes from the short list of rehab centers the hospital provided us with, because it seemed as though they would be able to meet my mother's needs and the public generally had positive experiences to report. After digging a little deeper, I can see that many positive reviews for this facility are over 3 years old. Clearly the quality has gone downhill! Following my first-hand experience at this facility, I must say that I would not recommend that anyone send his or her loved ones here. There are a few great workers here (mainly the two ladies at the front desk who had to put up with my incessant calling to try to get my questions answered), but the competence of the facility as a whole was completely unacceptable. I would not wish this added stress upon anyone, especially during a time when most people navigating this territory are already struggling to deal with the illness of a family member or loved one. I would strongly advise that you PICK ANOTHER FACILITY!

text: My husband's family is from Peru so we frequent Machu Picchu on the west side and Don Juan's Sandwiches quite often. Both restaurants changed ownership from Peruvian families to other Latin American families in the past 2-4 years, which made us concerned that the food quality would go down. I'm happy to say Don Juan's survived the switch! Our family normally shares an appetizer of Salchipapa (sliced hot dogs, fries, all covered in ketchup, mustard, and mayo), and I normally order El Desayuno Don Juan (Don Juan's Breakfast), a classic Peruvian breakfast that is so big, it's pretty much my lunch and dinner. It comes with sliced chicharron (pork), sliced camote (sweet potato), red onions, bread, and a tamale. You can ask for relleno (blood sausage) as well, and stuff all of that into the bread to make a sandwich, topped with aji (spicy sauce). My favorite sandwich is the torta de pescado (fish sandwich) but lomo saltado (juicy beef, tomatoes, and onions) is really good as well. Don't forget the ceviche! Yes, the owner is the cook for the entire restaurant, so don't expect super quick service. Latin American countries are known for their slower pacing when it comes to meals as it is a family affair and not just grab-and-go. The staff knows our family but even if they didn't, they're all friendly (and bilingual, so don't be intimidated if you don't know Spanish). Highly recommend!

text: I brought my Corvette here as Charlie was highly recommended by other Corvette drivers in the city. While speaking with him I noticed his professionalism and level of knowledge . I had a bad steering rack and the car had also been in need of an alignment . I'd had the car 3 years and never had one done . The damage that was done was my fault and I had made the mistake of driving it as well and unbeknownst to me I was circulating particles through the power steering system. Charlie had my car picked up the morning I called him. I was not in a hurry and he'd gotten the car on a Friday so it was the next week when the diagnosis came in. As I already knew the rack and pinion was bad .The rack had to be ordered but I was told I could find a used one or a remanufactured one my own if I had wanted to but I let them do that because , in all honestly , I was having trouble finding one. Now I looked around online at how to do this myself as I have worked on my own cars off and on over the years. This is not an easy job particularly because of how the steering shaft and sensors can get all thrown out of whack and damaged if you do it wrong which would be more problems. There is almost no clearance under their either and the rack is in there really tight. It was after reading these articles and looking at it from under the car myself that I decided to call Clearview Auto . All work was performed and he was able to save my power steering pump by doing a thorough flush and adding an additive to help it ( My Corvette is 22 years old!) . He showed me the four wheel alignment specs that he did on my car and how far it had been out . On the drive home I could tell that it drove straighter and took turns much more decisively . He gave me a computer print out to save showing me all of this . Now Charlie drives Corvettes himself and has driven just about every model they've made from C1 all the way up to C7 and he knows a lot about them but he can work on any brand of car from what I can tell based on some of the cars I saw around his shop. In talking to him you realize he knows a lot more than the average person does about cars. He will not give you a quickie short cut repair job to make a quick buck and send you on your way I suspect. He has a very thorough and in depth approach when he explains the issues and why he suggests what your car needs in my experience. There are plenty of shade tree self taught mechanics out there if that's the route you want to go but modern cars and sports cars are too complex for that almost any more. Many older repair shops don't even have alignment machines or other special equipment now required and will send you to a tire shop for one . At this shop your car is in very capable hands and I will take my truck here in the future.

text: 4.5 It took me a while to get there but I finally got there: beets. They're not just for tasting like dirt and tricking you in to thinking they're delicious. Now, while you won't catch me biting into one of these things like an apple, I no longer recoil in horror at the very mention. I can take a *light* amount of them in a salad. I'll plop a gentle amount on my plate at a family-style seating. But, if they're on a juice menu, I'm all in. Luckily for me, Twenty Two Juicery knows their way around making some delicious beet juice. Their main beet attraction is the Can't Beet It. It's been on the menu since the beginning and there's a good reason for it: it's delicious. The combo is not especially unique but the execution is beyond reproach. I'm not kidding when I say that this was one of the best juices I've ever had. I don't know whether it's the ratio of vegetables to fruit. I don't know whether it was the freshness of the produce. But something happened in that juicer to turn beet, carrot, apple, lemon, and ginger into just the recipe to give me a healthy pep to my step and load me up with all sorts of important vitamins and nutrients. I suppose there's not too much more to say. Wait! There is! Okay, Twenty Two is located in the Indianapolis City Market. I went there around the holidays... at lunch time. Yeah. I know. But do *you* know that the folks behind the counter kept a smile on their faces, engaged in chit chat and banged those orders out in no time? Despite having a line, they kept things moving and got people where they needed to go when they needed to get there. A good product, a smile and a sense of urgency... I like it, Twenty Two. I imagine that the juice here should be on/in every Indy City Market patrons' rotation. If not, get on board. It's a new year. Health is wealth... and delicious.

text: Well this is a hidden gem. 34 years in Reno and I've never been to Baldini's until now. Won Fleetwood Mask tickets on the radio so hubby and I decided to arrive early and have dinner at Occidental Tap House. Arrived at 6:00 on a Friday night and were seated promptly. Sports bar type atmosphere but very brightly lit. It's a large restaurant but the tables are spaced far apart which makes it seem kinda sparse. Large bar takes up a good amount of the place and there wasn't an empty seat. We were seated at a high table next to the bar and our waitress arrived quickly and took our drink order. Hubby ordered the Hefeweizen and I had the Kolsch. These are lighter refreshing German beers - no IPA's here which is fine with us. We really enjoyed the beers and at $3 for a pint during happy hour, they were a steal. We order the pretzel for an appetizer and it arrived soon after ordering. It's large enough to feed a crowd and is served hanging on a sort of frame and comes with 3 dips: beer cheese, curry ketchup and spicy mustard. It was tasty but just wish the cheese was served at a hotter temp. It was kinda lukewarm, but had a nice beer flavor. Not long after finishing the pretzel, our fish and chips arrived. If you're a fan, you will love these! 3 large pieces of cod, hand dipped in a beer batter. Perfectly crispy, large white filets. No fishy taste-very fresh. Served with crisp, thin fries and chipotle slaw. This slaw is not an after thought. It was so good, I ate it all. Our server, LeAnn, was terrific- she had a lot of tables but we never felt ignored. She was friendly without being overbearing. This place is a sports bar in a "workin stiff" area of town and felt very comfortable to us. By the way, the concert was great and I even won $100 at the nickel slots, so overall a great night. We're looking forward to our next visit!
